text:
Nina: quick RFC follow-up: propose we replace the bulky sidecar facade with a minimal probe-first handshake shim across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. keep responsibilities tiny: capability probe, routing hints, and transparent trace/request-id passthrough. no state, no request-mangling.

Omar: +1 on minimizing surface, but two blockers: (1) existing private HSM integrations rely on header injection; (2) streamed responses must be bit-for-bit compatible.

Nina: mitigation: operator-managed injection for private (helm + docs) so shim never holds secrets; for hosted/dedicated use short-lived token exchange via a dedicated authorizer. streaming parity enforced by replay diff harness.

Tess: rollout phases suggestion:
- alpha: hosted internal tenants (ff on)
- canary: hosted public with telemetry baselines
- beta: dedicated opt-ins (non-HSM)
- private: operator install + migration window
- GA flip after 90 days stable
include LB-level kill-switch to route back to legacy facade.

Felix: telemetry: preserve traceparent, X-Redwood-Req-Id, and add x-rw-shim-debug during canary. parity tests: short chat, long-context gen, embeddings at multiple TPS. thresholds: <3% p95 regression, no new 5xx classes.

Omar: add prompt-quality checks (sampled prompts diff / similarity for nondet routes) and a streaming-chunk binary diff tool. Also need manifest-lint rule to flag deprecated facade-only fields to avoid config drift.

Nina: compatibility handshake will include a tiny manifest (kv_layout, streaming_mode). shim will soft-fallback to legacy facade if incompatible and emit a 409 with migration hint when configured.

Tess: ops-bot create baseline + snapshot jobs?

ops-bot: created jobs: handoff-baseline-180500 (cadence=daily), handoff-snapshot-180500 (retention=30d). link: https://ci.redwood/handoff/180500

ci-bot: PR opened: "probe-shim: initial prototype + handshake" - https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/4920

Nina: I'll draft the rollout playbook, manifest linter spec, and operator helm snippet for private installs. ping @security for HSM review. thanks everyone. :rocket:
